answers.answer:
No. d1s9za_ (1s9z A:, sunid 98768, protein "Amyloidogenic design-1", sunid 103785) and d1hqja_ (1hqj A:, sunid 61142, protein "Unnamed design-1", sunid 100906) should not be called homologous, even though in SCOPe 2.08 they share the same family k.40.1.1 "Designed trimeric coiled-coil" (sunid 100905), the same superfamily k.40.1 (sunid 100904), the same fold k.40 (sunid 100903), and both are listed under species "Synthetic" (sunids 103786 and 64668).

The reason is the class. Both lineages terminate in class k "Designed proteins" (sunid 58788). Class k is a non-structural, non-evolutionary catch-all for de novo designed polypeptides; it is not one of the true structural classes (a through g), and its fold, superfamily, and family nodes do not carry the usual SCOP/SCOPe meaning. In the true classes, shared superfamily membership is the assertion of probable common ancestry and shared family membership (typically >30% identity or very strong structure/function evidence) is the assertion of clear homology. In class k, family and superfamily nodes merely group proteins that were designed to the same architectural concept, here a trimeric parallel coiled coil. Two independently designed synthetic peptides have no common ancestor, so there is no evolutionary homology to assert; any sequence resemblance (heptad-repeat hydrophobic patterning) reflects convergent design rules, not descent.

Consequences and limits: (1) Do not infer homology, shared ancestry, or function transfer between these two designed peptides from their k.40.1.1 co-membership; the 1s9z design is an amyloidogenic coiled-coil-to-beta switching peptide, while 1hqj is a different designed trimeric coiled coil, and the fact that both are in the same family says nothing about any shared functional behaviour. (2) Do not use either as a homology-modelling template for the other on the strength of the SCOPe classification; at most they are analogous coiled-coil structures. (3) Do not treat either as a representative of a natural coiled-coil family; class k entries are excluded from the kind of evolutionary reasoning SCOPe supports in classes a to g, and ASTRAL representative sets based on class k nodes are not evolutionary-family representatives. (4) If one needed to argue for any relationship, the required evidence would be external to SCOPe: the design papers themselves (showing whether one sequence was derived from the other), direct sequence alignment, and structural comparison; the SCOPe hierarchy alone cannot supply it. In summary: same family label, but in class k that label is a design-category annotation and not a statement of homology.
